$comment: Authored input for scripts/build-font-tracker.mjs. Derived fields (policy, bundle, measurements, parity) are never written here; this file holds owner-plan text, reconciled next actions, evidence keys, classes, scripts, style rules and in-flight candidates. Regenerate with: node scripts/build-font-tracker.mjs

ownerPlan.request: work this in as a tracker and to help prioritize work.
ownerPlan.summary: The owner completed 160 font-specific reviews: all 153 policy registry families plus seven shipped script-font dependencies missing from the registry. No repository files were changed by those reviews.

phases.title: Reconcile and baseline
phases.text: Reconcile the inventory and establish a fresh baseline. Record each font's selected name, preview face, version, hashes, available styles, scripts, and acceptance evidence.

phases.title: Loading and style coverage
phases.text: Finish loading and style coverage. Connect the shipped editor, gallery, browser, and Node hosts to the intended faces; eliminate unintended fallbacks.

phases.title: Aptos compatibility
phases.text: Prioritize Aptos and Aptos Display compatibility. Measure them separately and qualify candidates before adopting them.

phases.title: Remaining replacements
phases.text: Complete the remaining replacement work. Packaging, script shaping, and metric compatibility remain separate deliverables.

phases.title: Native verification and parity
phases.text: Complete native verification and rerun the full parity audit. Keep source, installed-package, and live-site claims separate.

rules: Every family gets its own fixture and acceptance record. Grouped rows share work, but a result for one family does not establish acceptance for another.
For proprietary fonts, PPTX always retains the user's selected name.
Preview replacements must use pinned, permitted files.
Metric qualification requires per-style measurements, matching line breaks and line metrics, and the unchanged geometry tolerances, not just a favorable average width.
The current Latin-only corpus must also be extended with script-specific text.

Most script packs currently provide regular and bold only. Required italic or other styles need genuine qualified faces; diagnostics preserve honesty but do not complete an outstanding fidelity requirement.
ownerPlan.criticalPath: Aptos and Aptos Display are the critical path: each appears in 704 of the 850 audited gallery values.

reconciliation: Aptos family (the owner's review predates this). Intos, Intos Display, Intos Narrow and Intos Serif measured 0.000% mean and maximum width delta in all four styles against Aptos 2.01, with equal vertical metrics and original (Inter-derived; serif Gelasio-derived) outlines under OFL-1.1 with no Reserved Font Name. They are the metric routes in policy (opf#166), vendored in opf-render (#54, `d528be5`, pinned commit `fef9315c`) and loaded lazily by browser hosts (opf-editor#42). Independently re-verified for Aptos, Aptos Display and Aptos Narrow; Aptos Serif was measured from Microsoft's Aptos Fonts download. The parity run on the merged mains passes all 704 Aptos and Aptos Display values, so they no longer lead the priority queue. Node and browser verification is recorded for the family; the editor playground test covers the Aptos scheme (Aptos and Aptos Display); the gallery editor waits for a release. The owner's "no verified compatible replacement" is superseded.

The committed parity run (opf#175 first, on the merged mains opf `338ddcd4` and opf-render `d528be5`: 660 perfect, 33 near and 157 mismatch, with fontResolution 733 pass, 31 near and 86 fail) is now the 2026-09-30 run on the published engines with the gallery editor font host modelled: 729 perfect, 108 near and 13 mismatch over 850 values, with fontResolution 755 pass, 92 near and 3 fail. Earlier runs are history.

Georgia now has a metric tier: Gelasio with liga and clig disabled (opf#163, opf-render#49, including the raster ZWNJ fix). The parity run on the merged mains reports it as a metric substitute for all 6 values.

Open families are now vendored from unmodified upstream or npm packages (opf-render#50): Open Sans, Montserrat (including 900), Poppins, Bebas Neue, PT Serif, Lora, Merriweather Sans, Source Sans 3 (with the Source Sans Pro alias), Red Hat Display (300, 400, 700) and Red Hat Text (400, 700). Raleway and Playfair Display are not bundled because resvg ignores the wght axis. The owner's "bundle" rows for the bundled families become verification work; FF-43 then bundled Anton, Archivo Narrow, Barlow, Bitter, EB Garamond, Figtree, Libre Caslon Text and Work Sans and completed Red Hat (see the FF-43 note below). The remaining bundling work is Liberation Mono, Sans and Serif, Playfair Display and Raleway.

Carlito is vendored as unmodified google/fonts files (opf-render#58) because its Reserved Font Name applies. Licenses, Reserved Font Names and no-hotlink rules are guarded in core and the renderer (opf#165, opf-render#53).

Script fonts: previews load script faces when the `scripts` option is passed (opf-render#55, opf-editor#40) and fall back per character to Noto Sans (opf-render#57). The parity run of 2026-09-30 models the gallery editor host (its font gate loads the script and vendored faces a document needs), so the 88 family uses it used to record as `missing` now resolve to their Noto route; loading is not verification per family. Still failing there: Raleway and Playfair Display (not bundled; the editor draws Roboto) and the Noto Sans Mongolian face, which cannot shape any text.

Hosts are recorded separately. The default Node registry (`prepareNodeFonts`) uses the `base` pack (Roboto and Roboto Mono only); the office-pack faces (Carlito, Arimo, Tinos, Cousine, Gelasio, Caladea, Intos) and the open pack load only when `pack: 'office'` is requested, and script faces only when the `scripts` option is passed. Browser hosts and the opf-editor playground load the 33 eager base and office faces and now load the vendored open pack and Intos lazily, on demand (opf-render#54, opf-editor#42). The gallery editor (a vendored opf-editor bundle) gets them only with a release that includes opf-editor#42, so it is recorded as pending, not as a gap in the family's status.

Gallery cards are a different host from the gallery editor. pptx-gallery self-hosts preview webfonts (pptx-gallery#53 and #54; replacement data in #51) for 49 families, including Anton, Barlow, Bitter, EB Garamond, Figtree, Libre Caslon Text, Work Sans, Playfair Display, Raleway, Open Sans and Montserrat, as upright regular and bold faces from pinned @fontsource packages or unmodified upstream files. The tracker reads that list from a pinned snapshot (`galleryCards`). Card previews do not change the editor's bundle, and no per-family card verification exists.

fontResolution treats a policy look-alike as near, not fail, when the PPTX names the selected family (opf#159). Parity harness fixes merged in opf#164 and opf#168. The value set is 850 after pptx-gallery#40 removed 50 unsupported chart types; Aptos and Aptos Display each appear in 704 of them.

Selawik 1.01 was measured and rejected as a Segoe UI replacement (opf#166: regular 0.16% mean and 2.51% max on the standard 300-string corpus, 0.73% and 9.7% on the reviewer's broader corpus); Red Hat Display stays the visual route. Segoe UI Light, Semilight and Semibold were measured separately.
Cover slide centering (opf-pptx#97) is geometry work with no font impact.

The seven shipped script-font dependencies missing from the registry (Noto Sans Arabic, Sinhala, Lao, Myanmar, Thaana, Syriac and Noto Serif Tibetan) are tracked as policy-gap records. Adding their policy rows is follow-up work: this change does not edit font-policy.json.

FF-43 (open replacement faces, opf-render branch claude/ff-43-bundle-open-candidates with this companion change): Barlow and Anton (google/fonts statics, byte-identical at commit 23e54b51ddff), Figtree, Work Sans, EB Garamond, Archivo Narrow, Libre Caslon Text and Bitter (npm-derived @expo-google-fonts statics, exact versions; no Reserved Font Name except Bitter, whose reserved name "Bitter Pro" is in no face name) are bundled with only the styles the policy needs, lazy in browser hosts; the eager list stays 33 faces. Red Hat Display now ships 300, 400, 600 and 700 with italics and Red Hat Text 400 and 700 with italics: the RedHatFont repository statics were unusable (the Regular, Light and SemiBold italics (and Red Hat Text Italic) do not set the OS/2 italic bit (only the Bold Italic files do), Red Hat Display SemiBold declares weight 707 and Bold 799 (Red Hat Text Bold declares 700), so a 600 request paints as Bold and the regular and bold italics as one face in resvg, probed), and Red Hat has no Reserved Font Name, so the correctly labelled @expo-google-fonts instances replace them. Libre Caslon Text has no bold italic upstream (explicit gap). The 19 rows whose route face was measured are re-measured (Rockwell on Bitter: 1.1% to 4.4% mean, up to 8.5% max) on 2026-09-29 against the installed Windows originals; the widths are unchanged (except Corbel and Gill Sans MT, which now follow the vendored Source Sans 3) and every row stays visual: none meets the metric bar. Grandview, Grandview Display, Tenorite and Tenorite Display are not installed on the measuring host and stay unmeasured. Trade-off: the shipped Red Hat Display Bold is about 2.5% narrower than the RedHatFont Bold it replaces (Segoe UI Bold preview mean width +0.6% to -1.8%, mean absolute 0.95% to 1.86%).

loading-gap.meaning: The family's preview face is not bundled by opf-render, so every host falls back to another face. A face that is bundled but not yet released to one host (the gallery editor) is noted in hostLoading and the next action, not counted as a gap.

style-gap.meaning: The preview face is bundled, but styles the family needs are missing from the bundle.

policy-gap.meaning: A face ships in the renderer but the family has no row in the font policy registry.

needs-special-path.meaning: No ordinary look-alike can serve the family: it needs a dedicated math, emoji or symbol-encoding path.

visual-gap.meaning: A bundled visual look-alike is routed, with styles present; metric qualification, appearance or measurement work remains.

script-gap.meaning: A bundled Noto script face is routed; native-script measurement, shaping, style and appearance qualification remain (the current corpus is Latin only).

baseline-needed.meaning: An open family is bundled with the styles it needs; a fresh per-host verification and acceptance record is the remaining work.

metric-measured.meaning: A metric-tier route measured against the real font in four styles on the source path (width bar met). Vertical metrics and line breaks are not yet recorded, and per-host and native verification remain, so it is not verified.

hostLoading.note: Derived from the pack a face ships in, the linked pull requests and the opf-render loaders. It is a source-level model, not a per-family verification. Vendored faces (the open pack and Intos) load lazily in browser hosts since opf-render#54 and opf-editor#42; the gallery editor gets them only with a release that includes opf-editor#42. Gallery cards (pptx.gallery self-hosted preview webfonts, pptx-gallery#53 and #54) are recorded separately as galleryCards from the pinned gallery snapshot.

Roboto Mono.reason: Code font. Italic faces exist upstream but are not bundled; the gap stays explicit until a gallery value needs them.

Bebas Neue.reason: Upstream ships a single upright face; unavailable styles must stay explicit rather than be synthesized.

Anton.reason: Upstream ships a single upright face; unavailable styles must stay explicit rather than be synthesized.

Noto Sans Mongolian.reason: Bold is required for parity with the other script packs; the pinned package ships regular only (owner: resolve the regular-only coverage).

Libre Caslon Text.reason: Upstream ships Regular, Italic and Bold only (no bold italic in the static releases or the Google Fonts instances); a bold italic request draws the real italic, reported visual, and bold is never synthesized.

Cambria Math.reason: Cambria Math ships one upright face (cambria.ttc); STIX Two Math and Noto Sans Math do too. Bold and italic requests take the regular face and are reported visual.

Segoe UI Emoji.reason: Segoe UI Emoji ships one face; Noto Color Emoji does too (colour glyphs have no weights).

Noto Color Emoji.reason: Colour emoji face (COLRv1 and OT-SVG); one face, no weights or italics exist.

Noto Emoji.reason: Monochrome emoji face used by the resvg raster path; the regular weight is pinned (upstream also ships 300 to 700).

STIX Two Math.reason: Math face with a MATH table; upstream ships one regular weight (STIX Two Text carries the text styles and is not bundled).

Noto Sans Math.reason: Math face with a MATH table; upstream ships one regular weight.

Aptos Mono.reason: Member of the Aptos family; Intos has no mono face, so it needs its own reference measurement alongside the family work.

Aptos.reason: Aptos family: critical path (owner phase 3). Measured metric in policy; host loading and verification wait on opf-render#54 and opf-editor#42, then a parity rerun.

Aptos Display.reason: Aptos family: critical path (owner phase 3). Measured metric in policy; host loading and verification wait on opf-render#54 and opf-editor#42, then a parity rerun.

Aptos Narrow.reason: Aptos family: critical path (owner phase 3). Measured metric in policy; host loading and verification wait on opf-render#54 and opf-editor#42, then a parity rerun.

Aptos Serif.reason: Aptos family: critical path (owner phase 3). Measured metric in policy; host loading and verification wait on opf-render#54 and opf-editor#42, then a parity rerun.

Aptos.nextAction: Intos is the merged metric route (opf#166; 0.000% mean and max in four styles against Aptos 2.01, vertical metrics equal, original Inter-derived outlines, OFL-1.1, no Reserved Font Name), vendored in opf-render#54 and loaded lazily in browser hosts (opf-editor#42). Then verify the gallery editor once a release includes opf-editor#42, rerun parity on the release, and confirm the PPTX still names the selected family in native PowerPoint. Roboto and Carlito stay alternates.

Then verify the gallery editor once a release includes opf-editor#42, rerun parity on the release, and confirm the PPTX still names the selected family in native PowerPoint. Do not inherit Aptos results.

Aptos.note: hhea, OS/2 typo and win, x-height and cap-height equal in all 16 styles; painted x-height and cap-height boxes agree (opf#166). Line breaks are not recorded. Weights 500, 600 and 800 resolve to Regular and Bold (FF-60: no upstream Medium or ExtraBold; the PPTX writes bold from 600, so PowerPoint draws the same two faces).
